chunks: And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to delay any obligatory fasts they had until the month of Shaban, out of reluctance to prevent the Messenger of Allah from his desire. And when Shaban arrived, they would fast, and the Prophet would fast with them.
And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to say, 'Shaban is my month.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the narrator of this tradition.
key_terms.حَاجَتَهُ: His desire or need, referring to marital relations.
key_terms.شَعْبَانُ: The eighth month of the Islamic month, noted here for its association with fasting and the Prophet.
key_terms.صِيَامٌ: Fasting, specifically referring to obligatory fasts in this context.

ai.seo_question: Why did the wives of the Prophet delay their fasts until Shaban?
ai.summary: This narration from Thawab al-A'mal highlights the Prophet's (peace be upon him) personal affinity for the month of Shaban, which Shia scholars interpret as a precursor to the spiritual preparation for Ramadan. The wives' practice of delaying obligatory fasts illustrates the balance between religious devotion and marital harmony, while the Prophet's declaration 'Shaban is my month' underscores its significance as a time of increased worship and anticipation of the coming month of fasting.
